quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Cause your engine to use too much oil.
Require your vehicle to need a tune-up sooner.
Make you feel sleepy while driving.
Start fires on grass along country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you feel sleepy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes poisonous gases, reduces noise, and cools hot gases from the engine. Fumes from a leaking exhaust system are dangerous and can cause death quickly. They can also make you drowsy while driving.

questions.question: Stopping completely at an intersection, letting cross traffic and pedestrians pass, and then going through when it is safe matches:

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let cross traffic and pedestrians pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars following too closely.
Go when the car ahead of you goes.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, look left first because cars from the left are closer to you. Then look right, and look left again to catch any cars you might have missed.

questions.question: Unless a sign says otherwise, the speed limit on an open county highway is:

options.text: 70 mph.
65 mph.
60 mph.
55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit on open county highways is normally 55 miles per hour. If a different speed limit is posted, follow that sign instead.

questions.question: To check your blind spots before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Use the outside rearview mirror.
Use both the inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head to check your blind spots before you change lanes.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the side of the road and look to see where it is.
Slow down but do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and look to see where it is.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: What colors are signs that show the distance to the next exit on a highway?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.correctAnswerText: Green with white letters
questions.explanation: Signs that give directions are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by other traffic. You should:

options.text: Drive slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Wait outside the intersection until you can go all the way through.
Use your horn to make cars move forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait outside the intersection until you can go all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is blocked on the other side and you cannot drive all the way through. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are dangerous.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are ideal.
The suggested speed to drive when conditions are ideal.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed under ideal conditions. You may drive slower than the posted limit, but you cannot drive faster. You must drive slower in school zones and work zones. If weather or road conditions make the posted speed unsafe, drive slower.

questions.question: While waiting to complete a left turn in an intersection, you should:

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
Drive around the back of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you turn or change lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels will keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What do pennant-shaped signs mean?

options.text: School zones.
No passing zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mean no passing zones. The sign will have text on it to confirm this.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is okay for drivers to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with just one rider.
A car driver must move completely into the other lane when passing a motorcycle.
A motorcycle's brake lights will turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car driver must move completely into the other lane when passing a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the full width of a lane. Make sure your car is completely in the left lane before you pass a motorcycle on the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
One-way traffic.
Limited parking.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Round signs mean a railroad crossing is ahead. Watch for trains.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time. What happens?

options.text: The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.
The car on the left has the right-of-way.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The left driver can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an uncontrolled intersection?

options.text: Keep your speed and go.
Stop, look both ways, and go.
Yield to all other drivers.
Be ready to yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or traffic light, be ready to yield to vehicles coming from the right. To do this, take your foot off the gas, get ready to brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road with traffic both ways, you must use the oncoming lane to pass. Only pass if it is safe and legal.

questions.question: If another car has high beams on and is coming toward you, where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road
The center of the road
The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: If another car has high beams on and won't dim them, look at the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on your path until the car passes.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of these except:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, time between drinks, and your weight. Being physically fit does not affect your BAC.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: A no passing zone
A one-way traffic area
The blind spot of a large vehicle
An area for motor vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot of a large vehicle
questions.explanation: "No zones" are the large blind spots around trucks and big vehicles. Smaller vehicles should avoid staying in these areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
A roundabout is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
Lanes are reserved for buses and carpool vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: What are regulatory signs?

options.text: They are placed everywhere there is danger.
They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn drivers about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular, white with black text. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. They show speed limits, no passing, no turning, and other rules.

questions.question: What should a driver do if their car with Anti-Lock Brakes starts to skid on a slippery road?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Lightly tap the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: If you lose traction, press the brake pedal hard and hold it while steering to safety. The Anti-Lock Braking System will pump the brakes automatically. Pumping the brakes yourself or releasing the pedal will turn off the system.

questions.question: What should you do if a green arrow changes to a solid green light?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You must stop turning and go straight.
You still have the right to turn.
You no longer need to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in that direction. However, you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass only from the lane next to the broken line.

questions.question: On a road without sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side as traffic direction.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road that faces oncoming traffic.
